clearedSpotChecks.check: The Q128 copy of mulDiv at pc 22358 (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:33 inside Position.update, src/libraries/Position.sol:93-96) and what its 512 bit branch can decide.
clearedSpotChecks.note: Position.sol:93-96 calls mulDiv with denominator FixedPoint128.Q128, and Pool.sol:189 is the only caller of position.update in src. prod1 is nonzero only when the product is at least 2^256, so the exact quotient is at least 2^128. FullMath.sol:30 passes because 2^128 exceeds prod1 for any such product below 2^384. Pool.sol:192 casts both results with toInt128, which reverts for 2^127 or more (SafeCast.sol:56-57). On a node that follows the specification the 512 bit branch therefore never writes state. A node fault that made this branch return a value below 2^127 would need a wrong quotient from a correct-looking prod0 and inverse, which the MULMOD battery and the v3 producer checks of this cycle cover. Reaching the branch needs about 2^128 fee units for one position, which only a token author can supply (pool-creator).

clearedSpotChecks.check: Planted faults in the reference used by the v3 style check, to show the check can fail.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I traced FullMath.sol:59-75 for an odd denominator: twos is 1 at line 59, line 73 gives (2^256-1)/1+1 which wraps to 0, so prod1*twos at line 75 is 0 and the result at line 99 depends only on prod0 after the remainder step. A wrong high half from MULMOD by 2^256-1 changes only the bound at line 30 and the branch at line 33, as the item says. raw/v3-4326.json shows 3,741 single512 matches, raw/v3-4326-plant.json shows 0 under the remainder fault and raw/v3-4326-planthi.json shows 2,840 under the high half fault, as stated. Under the remainder fault the count of 'single:target' matches rises from 11 to 1,618, so the alternative relations absorb some faulty cases; the 512 bit evidence still drops to zero, so the conclusion stands. The limit stated in the item (a high half fault that keeps prod1 nonzero and below the denominator is invisible for odd denominators) is a real gap for the v4 fee division at SwapMath.sol:65-74 and 104, whose denominators 1e6 and 1e6 minus fee are even, and for the Q96 and Q128 copies, whose denominators are powers of two where twos is the whole denominator and the flip at line 73 moves prod1 into the result.
